negative_results.explanation: Against the same mill, cutter and battery packs run greedily, SinchaiSlot with the groundwater cap uses -1.0% solar energy (P10 -1.2% to P90 -0.4%): the planner does not add sun on its own; the extra loads do. Its gains are elsewhere: Gini of access 0.27 vs 0.39, and the cap held in 100% of runs vs 0%.

budget_tradeoff.explanation: The cap holds back 4,665 m3 of solar water a year, so SinchaiSlot avoids 14.2% less diesel than the per-m3 operator model without a cap; that water goes to diesel sellers on the same aquifer unless they share the cluster budget.

statements: Against the same mill, cutter and battery packs run greedily, SinchaiSlot with the groundwater cap uses -1.0% solar energy (P10 -1.2% to P90 -0.4%): the planner does not add sun on its own; the extra loads do. Its gains are elsewhere: Gini of access 0.27 vs 0.39, and the cap held in 100% of runs vs 0%.
Without the cap the planner uses +0.9% solar energy vs greedy dispatch and meets 31% of tenant need.
By season (one village, first held-out year): +2.4% vs greedy loads in monsoon weeks, -0.9% in the rest of the year, when water demand fills the pump and the cap holds water back.

The cap holds back 4,665 m3 of solar water a year, so SinchaiSlot avoids 14.2% less diesel than the per-m3 operator model without a cap; that water goes to diesel sellers on the same aquifer unless they share the cluster budget.
The solar forecast adds +0.9% over planning on yesterday's sun; a perfect forecast would add +2.1% more.
